sources.title: Exact repository axis0 mean/variance question and verified mapping
Independent source-first axis0 statistics candidate review

claims.text: The source asks for mean and variance on the first dimension but does not preserve Data shape/type, axis convention, population-vs-sample definition, missing-value policy or API.
Under the explicit rectangular finite double[][]/axis0/population-variance contract, per-column Welford state computes mean and M2 in one pass.
The exact fixture validates normal, single-row, large-offset, shape, finite-value and immutability cases.
Independent source-first review found no hard failures, unsupported claims or uncovered preserved-source variants and revalidated the exact Welford fixture.

findings: The preserved source asks only for mean and variance on the first dimension; it does not fix Data shape/type, axis convention, population-vs-sample denominator, missing-value behavior, output shape or language/API.
The candidate explicitly labels rectangular finite double[][], row/axis-0 aggregation, per-column output, population variance and rejection of ragged/non-finite input as answer-side contracts.
The exact fenced Java equals the saved fixture and independently re-passes ordinary, single-row, large-offset, shape, finite-value and input-immutability checks under JDK 21.

The Welford invariant and numerical-stability motivation are relevant and bounded: the answer does not claim floating-point error disappears and it distinguishes the sample-variance and NaN-handling variants.
